In the matter of : Mahammad Ali @ Ali
 ......Petitioner/
 Appellant.
 Mr. Sourav Chatterjee, Sr. Adv,
 Mr. Simanta Kabir,
 Mr. Avik Pramanick ......for the Appellant/
 Petitioner.
Mr. Partha Pratim Das  Mr. S. S. Saha .......for the State.
Dictated by Arijit Banerjee, J.
In re : CRAN 2 of 2025 1.
In spite of service of notice, nobody appears for the victim/defacto complainant.
2. The petitioner was convicted under Sections 376/417 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for ten years.
He says that he is in custody about for two years eight months.
He further says that the evidence on record will clearly bring out that the victim girl had consensual physical relationship with him.
The victim girl herself has deposed that she continued to cohabit with him for five years.
The victim girl gave birth to a child.
The petitioner is not the father.
When the petitioner denied fatherhood, the problem started and a false complaint was lodged.
He prays for suspension of sentence.
3. Learned State Counsel strongly opposes the prayer.
He says that there is a DNA report confirming that the petitioner is the father of the child to whom the victim girl gave birth.
The girl was a minor at the time of the alleged offence.
Consent of a minor is of no legal consequence.
There is sufficient incriminating evidence to support the conviction.
Hence, the petitioner's prayer should not be allowed.
4. We have considered the rival contentions of the parties.
We find that there are two DNA reports on record.
The first DNA report did not hold the petitioner to be the father of the child.

Secondly,
the victim girl herself deposed that she continued to cohabit with the petitioner for five years.
Prima facie, there appears to be a consensual physical relationship between the petitioner and the victim girl.
The age of the victim girl at the time of occurrence also prima facie seems to be in doubt.

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid, we find that the petitioner has made out a prima facie arguable case for acquittal at the hearing of the appeal.
Accordingly, we are inclined to allow this application and suspend the sentence of imprisonment imposed upon the applicant/appellant.

7. Accordingly, we direct that the applicant/appellant, namely Mahammad Ali @ Ali shall be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.10,000/-, with two sureties of like amount each, one of whom must be local, to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Rampurhat and on further conditions that he shall not enter the jurisdiction of Murarai Police Station until further order and shall inform his current local address where he will be residing presently to the learned Trial Court and shall meet the Inspector in charge/Officer in charge of the jurisdictional police station once in a fortnight till disposal of the appeal and shall not leave the District of Birbhum until further order except for the purpose of attending Court proceedings.

The applicant shall be personally present or shall be represented by his Counsel during hearing of the appeal and he shall surrender before the Trial Court as and when called for in connection with the present appeal.

8. The department is directed to forward a copy of this order to the Superintendent of the concerned Correctional Home for immediate release of the applicant/appellant unless he is wanted in connection with any other case.

9. We clarify that the observations made by us in this order are only for the purpose of disposing of the application for suspension of sentence and the same shall have no relevance at the final hearing of the appeal.
10. The application being CRAN 2 of 2025 is accordingly disposed of.
11. All parties shall act in terms of server copy of the order downloaded from the official website of this Court.
(Apurba Sinha Ray, J.)
(Arijit Banerjee, J.)
